subject: Intermittent 503s & latency spike on inference endpoints — NAT translation / DNS investigation
messages:

Subject: Intermittent 503s and high latency across inference endpoints

Hi Priya / Marissa,

We started seeing a spike in 503s and request latency for our inference routes around 07:50 Eastern. Rough sample attached (client-logs-503s.txt) — ~17% of calls are returning 503s and the median latency jumped from ~120ms to 900ms for the same client region. The issue is impacting checkout personalization and we've started throttling client retries to avoid duplicate charges.

Quick details:
- Affected endpoints: /v1/infer/* across eu-west-1 region
- First observed: ~07:48-07:52 ET (rolling)
- Impact: 10-25% error rate on production traffic, large latency variance

We've opened a ticket on our side and can provide packet captures or sproc logs if helpful. Please advise immediate mitigations — our execs are asking for an ETA.

Thanks,
Liam O'Neil
Head of Platform Engineering
BrightBasket

Subject: Re: Intermittent 503s and high latency across inference endpoints

Quick findings from an initial probe: attaching a short pcap (pcap-sample.pcap). Observations:
- We saw a surge in TCP retries from BrightBasket IP blocks to our eu-west-1 egress nodes beginning ~07:48 ET.
- NAT translation session table on three egress NAT gateways reached ~92% capacity, coincident with spikes. When entries are evicted prematurely in that window, connections get reset and client libraries surface 503s.
- DNS: observed sporadic NXDOMAIN and TTL inconsistencies for one of our internal resolver clusters servicing eu-west-1 — likely causing clients to re-resolve and create connection bursts. Not the primary failure but amplifying the issue.
- No CPU/GPU saturation on model-serving machines; server-side telemetry shows normal token-per-second rates.

Immediate mitigations we applied (08:36–08:50 ET):
1) Increased conntrack table size on the three impacted NAT gateways (temporary bump).
2) Temporarily relaxed a strict firewall state timeout for ephemeral ports from 30s -> 120s for BrightBasket's IP range.
3) Rebalanced a subset of BrightBasket flows to a different egress pool to distribute translations.

Effect: error rate dropped from ~17% -> ~5% within 10 minutes and median latency reduced to ~220ms but not back to baseline. Still monitoring.

Next steps:
- Collect full packet capture for the full 07:40–08:10 window (requesting from BrightBasket).
- Root cause: likely combination of translation-session exhaustion + resolver inconsistency. We'll do a post-incident audit of conntrack growth by flow and TTL anomalies.

Attaching: pcap-sample.pcap (5MB excerpt)

—Rishi
Principal Network Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Rishi: please prepare a one-slide summary outlining the root cause hypothesis and a short remediation plan (patching schedule + risk). Marissa: prep notes for customer communications and an ETA on formal postmortem.

I'll raise a priority for a permanent fix: either dynamic conntrack autosizing for egress gateways or a stateless translation path where feasible — engineering will size implement risk/effort after investigation.

Subject: RE: Intermittent 503s and high latency across inference endpoints — remediation & next steps

Liam — quick update and next steps following today's mitigation window: the temporary changes reduced the error rate and latency but we are treating this as an incident requiring root cause analysis.

Status:
- Immediate impact: error rate decreased to ~3–6% after conntrack bump + flow rebalance.
- Short-term mitigation: full rollout of the conntrack parameter change to all egress NATs (scheduled 13:30 ET, low-risk).
- Medium-term actions (owned):
  * Network (Rishi): audit conntrack growth patterns, implement autosize policy for peak tail, and harden firewall state timeouts where appropriate. Target: complete pilot by 2027-12-08.
  * Infra (Vivek/eng): evaluate a hybrid stateless translation path for hot flows; initial feasibility review by 2027-12-10.
  * CS (Marissa/Priya): customer-facing postmortem and compensation eligibility review. Draft postmortem targeted 2027-12-03.

Requested from BrightBasket: full packet capture for 07:40–08:10 ET and confirmation whether any client-side retries or SDK updates were deployed in last 48 hours.

Bridge: 11:00 ET today confirmed for exec sync (join link shared separately).

Attachment: remediation-checklist.md (short checklist), JIRA-RED-4321 created for tracking.

Thanks again for the quick collaboration — we'll follow up with a formal postmortem and timeline for permanent fixes.

—Priya
